AND THOU SHALT SMITE ON THE ROCKE, AND WATER SHALL COME OUT OF IT, THAT THE PEOPLE MAY DRINKE (plate, page 55) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS

MOSES THEN CAME AND CALLED FOR THE ELDERS OF THE PEOPLE, AND PROPOSED UNTO THEM ALL THESE THINGS, WHICH THE LORDE COMMANDED HIM (plate, page 63) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS
THOU SHALT ALSO ANOINT AARON AND HIS SONNES, AND SHALT CONSECRATE THEM THAT THEY MAY MINISTER UNTO ME IN THE PRIESTS OFFICES (plate, page 67) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS

THEN ALL THE PEOPLE PLUCKT FROM THEMSELVES THE GOLDEN EARERINGS, AND THEY BROUGHT THEM UNTO AARON WHO RECEIVED THEM AT THEIR HANDES, AND FASHIONED IT, AND MADE OF IT A MOLTEN CALFE (plate, page 75) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS
MOSES WRATH WAXED HOTE, AND HE CAST THE TABLES OUT OF HIS HANDES, AND BRAKE THEM IN PIECES BENEATH THE MOUNTAINE (plate, page 79) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS
HE WROTE IN THE TABLES THE WORDES OF THE COVENAUNT, EVEN THE TEN COMMANDEMENTS (plate, page 83) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS
THEN THE DAUGHTER OF PHARAOH OPENED THE ARKE, AND SAWE IT WAS A CHILDE (plate, page 15) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS

THEN MOSES ASSEMBLED ALL THE CONGREGATION OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL, AND SAYDE UNTO THEM, "THESE ARE THE WORDES WHICH THE LORDE HATH COMMANDED THAT YE SHOULDE DOE THEM" (plate, page 87) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS

BEZALEEL MADE TWO CHERUBIMS OF GOLDE, AND THE CHERUBIMS SPREAD OUT THEIR WINGS, THEIR FACES WERE ONE TOWARDS ANOTHER. LIKEWISE HE MADE THE CANDLESTICKE OF PURE GOLDE (plate, page 91) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS
MOREOVER THEY MADE GARMENTS OF MINISTRATION TO MINISTER IN THE SANCTUARIE; THEY MADE ALSO THE HOLY GARMENTS FOR AARON, AS THE LORDE HAD COMMANDED MOSES (plate, page 95) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS
AND MOSES BEHELD ALL THE WORKE, AND BEHOLDE, THEY HAD DONE IT AS THE LORDE HAD COMMANDED; AND MOSES BLESSED THEM (plate, page 99) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS

AND IN THOSE DAYES, WHEN MOSES WAS GROWEN, HE WENT FOORTH UNTO HIS BRETHREN, AND LOOKED ON THEIR BURDENS (plate, page 19) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS
THEN THE ANGEL OF THE LORDE APPEARED UNTO HIM IN A FLAME OF FIRE, OUT OF THE MIDDLE OF A BUSH; AND HE LOOKED AND BEHOLDE, THE BUSH WAS NOT CONSUMED (plate, page 23) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS
HE CAST THE RODDE ON THE GROUND, AND IT WAS TURNED INTO A SERPENT, AND MOSES FLED FROM IT (plate, page 27) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS
THEN THE LORDE SAYDE UNTO AARON, "GOE MEETE MOSES IN THE WILDERNESSE." AND HE WENT AND MET HIM IN THE MOUNT OF GOD AND KISSED HIM (plate, page 31) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS
SO WENT MOSES AND AARON, AND GATHERED ALL THE ELDERS OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL (plate, page 35) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS
THEN AFTERWARD MOSES AND AARON WENT AND SAYDE TO PHARAOH, "THUS SAYETH THE LORDE GOD OF ISRAEL, LET MY PEOPLE GOE" (plate, page 39) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS
THEN MOSES STRETCHED FOORTH HIS HANDE TOWARDE HEAVEN, AND THERE WAS A BLACKE DARKENESSE IN ALL THE LANDE OF EGYPT (plate, page 43) from THE STORY OF THE EXODUS

Art (Arthur) Paul (b. January 18, 1925 in Chicago, Illinois) is an American graphics designer and the designer of the Playboy bunny.

Paul studied at the Art Institute of Chicago (1940-1943) and at the Institute of Design [Illinois Institute of Technology](1946-1950). He was working as a freelance designer when he in 1953 was contacted by playboy founder Hugh Hefner who needed a logo for his new magazine. He created the now famous rabbit wearing a tuxedo bow tie. Paul went on to design the whole first edition of the magazine and was hired by Hefner as Playboy's first art director in 1954, a position he held for 30 years.

In 1986 Paul was elected to the Hall of Fame of the Art Directors Club of New York.

Title: I find a sense of freedom in the suburbs…. You assume the mask of suburbia for outward appearances and yet no one knows what you really do.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Title: It's a great pleasure to watch yourself make love in the six dozen mirrors that line the ceilings and walls. I've spent a tremendous amount of thought and planning to get the total effect of the bedroom., It's fascinating to watch our friends' reactions to seeing the luxury and sensuousness of the room. Our bedroom is the most enjoyable room in the house.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Title: We feel most people have the wrong attitude about sex, that it's nasty and to be only in the dark. With us sex takes care of itself.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Title: I get a lot of compliments on the front room wall. I like Italian Syrocco floral designs over the mantle. It goes with the Palos Verde rock fireplace.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Title: I believe in women's liberation. I'm tired of the image of the women who has the most sanitary toilet bowl, the cleanest floor, and the brattiest kids as the supermother., I want to be able to change with my children and to change with my life as I grow older. Staying at home and taking care of the kids doesn't help.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Title: A lot of people say we're chunks of meat, like cattle, but we're not. We're all individuals with dreams and aspirations like everybody else. Being a beauty contestant has taught me about myself, other people, poise and public speaking., If I had it to do over again, I would.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Title: I've been a chiropractor for thirty-three years, working directly and indirectly with nerves through the spinal column. I'm thinking of retiring in a couple of years and going into worm farming. Worms are an asset to society.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Title: Some days when there is no one to play with I build Glenn a tent play house out of two chairs and two blankets.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Title: We really enjoy living in a mobile home. My hobby is collecting coins and my wife plays her Wurlitzer for entertainment.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Title: We really enjoy getting together with our friends to drink and dance. It's a wild party and we're having a great time.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Title: I really enjoy being here because it's my pleasure to help people. They'd have to fire me before I'd quit. I know I'm loved and vice versa.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Title: I've been a UPI correspondent, a publicist for an Italian film producer, a writer for the U.S. Army, a public relations man and an operations manager for record stores. Now I'm promotion and marketing director for a newspaper chain., Within a year, I'll be off to Turkey. It will be a jumping-off place. The world will be my oyster.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Title: Like everyone else, I'm caught up in the rat race. I work eighty hours a week and with my real estate investments earn $100,000 a year. I just got divorced., In the insurance business the public thinks we promise the moon but we can only deliver half a moon.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Title: Television cameramen are a special breed. When you read something in a book you say that's someone's opinion. When you see it on TV you say that's gospel. I have one minute, thirty seconds to make a statement., It had to be accurate, it has to be the truth.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Title: Mardi Gras is an annual fund-raising event staged by the Pleasanton Juniors. King and Queen Candidates hold moneymaking events and the candidate who raises the most money wins., Last year we raised $12,800 for the senior citizens' transportation system and $1,000 for youth counseling programs. The climax is the Mardi Gras Ball. Over 500 people come to drink, eat, dance and celebrate the coronation.
CreditLine: Gift of Robert Harshorn Shimshak and Marion Brenner

Upper panel with inlays of colored calf in pink and burgundy to form the title 'labon / fam / abe / ber' in stylized letters, several letters with inset circular and semi-circular sections of smooth white card, with erotic details from the plates in the book. Café crème brushed suede doublures; matching calf-backed, suede-lined cloth chemise and slipcase. On "papier d'Indochine."
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: Je Ne Mange Pas De Ce Pain-Là (I don't eat that kind of bread) [I want no part of it]
Medium: Number 26 from the edition of 25 author's copies (numbered from 17 to 41). 28 poems by Péret in letterpress; frontispiece etching by Ernst. On "le Roy Louis teinte bourgogne" paper, with the original etching frontispiece on chine. Also inserted loose, the original subscription leaf
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: Je Sublime
Medium: Octavo, 28 pages including four original frottage prints by Ernst, thirteen poems by Péret, in original publisher's cream-colored wrappers, uncut signatures. One of only fifteen édition de tête on Japon Impérial paper. Each frottage unique
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: An intervention into Knaurs Jugend Lexikon  [Knaurs Children's Encyclopedia]
Medium: Unique artist’s book. 86 pages. Feldmann’s name printed in autograph in capital letters at the top of page 3; dates in autograph on page 4. Hundreds of cut-out magazine reproductions, each spread consisting of multiple layers of imagery, each glued along the top, thus when lifted others are revealed beneath. Blue cloth, blind-stamped
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: Bilder (Portfolios 1-4)
Medium: Sextodecimo (varying sizes) staple-bound, black-and-white half-tone photographs; stamped ("FELDMANN") cardboard wrappers. Includes an original handwritten letter from 1972 from the artist to the previous owner Dietmar Kirves, which illuminates his criteria for the Bilder project
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: L'Air de l'Eau (The Air of Water)
Medium: Quarto; 24 unnumbered folios; four engravings by Alberto Giacometti housed in unique livre-objet binding by Georges Hugnet. Deluxe edition; one of five copies on Japan nacré paper
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: La Guitare Endormie. Contes et Poémes (The Sleeping Guitars: Stories and Poems)
Medium: Octavo, frontispiece portrait of Reverdy by Gris. 37 poems illustrated with three monochrome illustrations by Gris, each with additional coloring by hand. Unique full turquoise, polished calf binding by Georges Leroux with his signature in gilt and dated 1967. Boards and spine with elaborate decorative collage resembling a Cubist work by Gris composed of wooden inserts, gilt tooling and inlaid polished calf sections, in a variety of colors and forms with additional crushed Morocco. Gold leaf and black calf lettering, title gilt to spine, suede-lined calf-backed wooden board chemise with gilt title to spine, and matching slipcase. Issued with an original pencil drawing for one of the reproductions, and an original folded manuscript of one of the poems by Pierre Reverdy
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: Ana and Carl and some other couples
Artist: Nicolás Guagnini, Leigh Ledare, PPP Editions, New York
Medium: Quarto; 256 pages printed on an Indigo digital press; bound without covers and printed on perforated paper; wrapped in a black glassine paper affixed with a wafer seal
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: Four Poems including "Non Vouloir"
Artist: Pablo Picasso, Marcel Duchamp, Joan Miró, Valentine Hugo
Medium: "Non Vouloir" bound together with three other poems: "Pablo Picasso," "Marcel Duchamp," and "Au Dépens du mots." Each from the édition de tête of 6 copies on japon nacré, bound together in a signed binding painted by Hugnet and each with a presentation to Paul Eluard.
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: Poésie de Mots Inconnus
Medium: Letterpress text by various poets throughout, several sheets with additional overprinting in color, each illustrated by various artists with linocut, woodcut, lithograph, etching, burin engraving or drypoint. The folded copy, loose as issued in paper wrappers, covered with vellum wrappers with a stamped vignette on the front by Ribemont-Dessaignes and titled “Ne coupez pas mes pages” [Don’t cut my pages], enveloped in a two-part vellum packet with the blind-stamped titled on the spine. "COMPAGNON XV OSCAR DOMINGUEZ" printed in violet on the colophon
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: ray gi[ve]s ANOTHER PA[rt]y
Medium: Small quarto; 28 pages of collage made from newspaper and magazine images and autograph text
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: A Book About Death
Medium: Estimated edition of 500. A complete set of 13 pages (pages numbered 1-15, but 13-14 were never produced). Folded loose-leaf, black and white offset on typing paper
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: La fin du monde filmée par l'ange de N.-D.
Medium: Compositions en Couleurs par Fernand Léger. Quarto, 22 designs by Fernand Léger including those for the cover, 25 leaves with added pochoir decoration; original publisher's printed wrappers and backstrip retained; full blue crushed morocco over boards with elaborate gilt decorative tooling, gilt title to spine, green morocco-edged brushed suede endpapers; marbled paper chemise and matching slipcase. Deluxe, large paper édition de tête on papier de Rives à la forme, one of only 25 copies. This in a unique binding by Paul Bonet, signed in gilt and dated ‘1950;’ with additional proof material
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: Industriia sotsializma
Medium: Seven volumes, quarto; gravure plates. An abundance of fold-outs, gate-folds, and accordion folds, collages, and cut-outs; printed on a variety of paper types. Six separately bound books in wrappers, each numbered one to six and with its own photographic images and embossed designs on the cover. One folder labeled "seven" with fold-out map laid in. Photographically illustrated canvas slipcase
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: Untitled (Walls paper)
Medium: Unique artist’s book; oblong octavo, color illustrations, several fold-outs and split pages, black-and-white printed wrappers, staple-bound
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: Annette Messager collectionneuse: Les approches
Medium: Vertical oblong quarto; four folded, cream-colored board folios, with 19 mounted gelatin silver photographs; hand-written texts in ink. Housed in gray cloth folder with hand-written name and title on spine in black marker; black-cord tie. First and only edition, one of 30 copies, signed and numbered by the artist in black marker on the colophon. Chemise interior is lined with off-white paper. The last image in each of the four sequences is enhanced with graphite by the artist
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: FotoZeit Salzau
Medium: Oblong vertical octavo; 9 folders; 35 original vintage prints tipped-in. Title printed on paper label affixed to black cloth slipcase
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: Enfances
Medium: Quarto; untitled poems by Georges Hugnet with three etchings by Joan Miró. Housed in a vellum binding with a unique watercolor and ink drawing by Miró on the front panel and a line drawing by Miró on the rear panel. One of 95 copies in the edition printed on Vélin D’Arches - only 50 were realized
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: A Toute Épreuve
Medium: Suites issued on chine; this copy also includes the original publisher's announcement, loosely inserted. Folio; 55 unnumbered leaves, 27 folded sheets, 1 inserted single sheet. Illustrated with 80 color woodcuts by Miró - four conceived as double-page spreads including that for the cover. Loose as issued in original publisher's cream printed wrappers with Miró's woodcut, separate wrapper for the suite, parchment-backed wooden board chemise with gilt title to spine and matching slipcase. Edition of 130 on Arches; one of 20 copies with a separate suite of the woodcuts hors-texte on chine and an additional woodcut-printed in black only, with gouache heightening by Miró
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: 5人の片眼の兵隊 (Gonin no Katame no Heitai [Five One-Eyed Soldiers])
Medium: Octavo; 12 leaves laid into a small folding portfolio, 1 duplicate leaf; 1 original etching, engravings, 1 original gelatin silver print by Narahara tipped-in, poetry by Ikeda
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: Sei illustrazioni per gli scritti sull'arte antica di Johann J. Winckelmann
Medium: Folio; six double-page illustrations printed in lithography and silkscreen; paper over boards, typographic dust jacket, glassine wrapper; housed in the original printed board folder with ties, label affixed to recto
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: Le Chef-d’œuvre inconnu
Medium: Folio; illustrated with 13 etched plates by Picasso. Full dark brown crushed Morocco leather by Georges Cretté with his signature in gilt, with matching chemise and slipcase. CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: Non Vouloir
Medium: Small octavo collection of poems by Hugnet; bound in a full red-leather binding. In addition this copy is accompanied by the four original zinc plates. Unique copy of the deluxe edition of four printed on chine paper
CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell

Title: La Maigre
Medium: Vellum wrapper. CreditLine: Promised gift of Helen and Sam Zell
